interpretation: Sound bends one of Livia's cast-silver rings. Time runs along the metal from one end of the open ring to the other; pitch lifts the band along the finger, level swells it outward, pitch slope leans it. Every point keeps its angle, may only move outward from the finger and may slide along the finger, so the map is one-to-one: the piece cannot tear or pass through itself. Casting checks then decide how far it may go. Lift moves whole cross-sections and keeps the silver's weight, so it carries most of the change; swell adds silver and closes lattice gaps fastest, so it is weighted 0.4, as is lean.
